author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: In Nebula or OneView, go to Settings > Syslog Logging, pick a Windows endpoint as the syslog communication endpoint, and point it at the data collector over TCP or UDP (TLS isn't offered). Malware, PUP, PUM and Ransomware detections go to Antivirus; EDR Suspicious Activity, Exploit, Remote Intrusion and Website detections go to the third-party alert schema. Category names and their short forms (arw, ae, rid, mwac) both work. The event time is rt, the detection time, because the endpoint polls the console every few minutes and buffers up to 24 hours. Hashes are read from msg. Only Suspicious Activity has a per-event severity (cs2); the header severity is one fixed setting, so other alerts get HIGH, or MEDIUM for websites. ThreatDown publishes no example line for Remote Intrusion, Exploit, Ransomware or Suspicious Activity, so those samples follow the documented field table. In a lab tenant on 2026-10-13 the engine kept CEF's \n escape in msg as two characters, so the parsers accept both forms, and it also stored event_type and sensor_version on the antivirus records, fields its antivirus schema has but the docs' table doesn't list. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test there, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines. On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent. No built-in parser in that tenant matched these lines.
